newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban official sees nickel output doubling by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Cuban official sees nickel output doubling by 2000.

text.p: Cuban Foregn Investment Minister Ibrahim Ferradaz forecast Wednesday that the island could be producing some 100,000 tonnes of nickel a year by the end of the decade.
Production last year was a record 53,600 tonnes in a sector that slumped sharply in the early 1990s and has rebounded rapidly in the last two years.

Ferradaz was speaking at a conference on the Cuban economy attended by foreign business people and addressed by senior government ministers. The meeting was closed to the media but a copy of his speech was obtained by reporters.
Ferradaz noted that Cuba currently has three operating nickel plants, all in the northeast of the island. He said a fourth would be operational soon, without giving a date.
Ferradaz added that the process of building a fifth plant should start before the end of the decade.
"At this time the northeastern area of the country will be producing more than 100,000 tonnes of nickel," he said.

Ferradaz was speaking in the context of new possibilities for investors in Cuba. He cited the island's three current leading foreign exchange earners -- tourism, sugar and nickel -- as being areas that were in expansion and would continue to need foreign investment.
